Enabling `getopts` without `html` breaks the binary build Location: `pulldown-cmark/src/main.rs:25`; supporting configuration: `pulldown-cmark/Cargo.toml:27`. Expected: an enabled binary has its required dependencies. Observed: `cargo check --locked -p pulldown-cmark --no-default-features --features getopts` fails with unresolved import `pulldown_cmark::html`. The binary requires only `getopts`, although it unconditionally imports the feature-gated renderer. Consequence: this selectable package configuration cannot build. Require both features for the binary, or make the CLI feature enable HTML. Add this configuration to build checks. ## Major ### 2. CLI input and output failures are mishandled Locations: `pulldown-cmark/src/main.rs:172`, `:184`, `:219`. Expected: unsuccessful reads or writes produce a diagnostic and unsuccessful exit status. Executed probes found: - Invalid UTF-8 stdin: empty output, exit **0**. - Output redirected to `/dev/full`: exit **0**. - Missing input file: panic, exit **101**. Consequence: pipelines can report success despite producing no usable output. Propagate I/O errors consistently, return a result from the rendering helper, and explicitly flush its `BufWriter`; drop-time flush errors otherwise remain invisible. ### 3. Processing multiple files repeats earlier content Location: `pulldown-cmark/src/main.rs:167`. Expected: each file contributes its contents once. Observed: files containing `Alpha\n` and `Beta\n` produce: ```html

Alpha

Alpha Beta

``` `read_to_string` appends to the reused buffer, which is rendered after every file. Consequence: batch conversion duplicates content and can merge unrelated Markdown structures. Clear the buffer per file, or concatenate all inputs and render once. Add a two-file CLI regression. ### 4. CRLF becomes two spaces inside code spans Location: `pulldown-cmark/src/parse.rs:1340`. Expected: CommonMark treats CRLF as one line ending, converted to one space inside a code span. Observed: input `` `a\r\nb` `` produces `a b`; LF and standalone CR produce one space. The same problem occurs inside blockquotes. Consequence: Windows-authored Markdown changes code text. Consume the complete line ending using `scan_eol`, then append one space. Extend the existing newline-in-code tests with CRLF. ### 5. A trailing tab prevents a code fence from closing Location: `pulldown-cmark/src/scanners.rs:528`. Expected: CommonMark permits spaces or tabs after a closing fence. Observed: `"```\ncode\n```\t\nafter\n"` renders the closing fence and `after` inside the code block. Consequence: an ordinary trailing tab changes the remainder of the document’s structure. Scan both spaces and tabs before checking the line ending; test both fence characters. ### 6. Case-insensitive footnote matches produce broken HTML links Locations: `pulldown-cmark/src/html.rs:53`, `:139`; related reference emission: `pulldown-cmark/src/parse.rs:768`. Expected: references accepted as matching the same definition share its destination and number. Observed: ```markdown ref [^FOO] [^foo] [^foo]: Note ``` produces references to `#FOO` numbered 1 and `#foo` numbered 2, while only `id="foo"` exists. Unicode case-folding variants also receive separate numbers and unmatched destinations. Consequence: accepted footnote references fail to navigate and display inconsistent numbering. Resolve references to a canonical definition identifier and use the same case-folded identity for numbering. Add ASCII and Unicode case-variant tests. ### 7. Standalone CR line endings are inconsistently recognized Location: `pulldown-cmark/src/scanners.rs:508`. Expected: CommonMark accepts LF, CRLF, and standalone CR. Observed: `scan_nextline` searches only for LF. With heading attributes enabled, `"# heading\r\rpara\r"` becomes one heading containing the following paragraph. Executed probes also found incorrect fenced-code, indented-code, and HTML-block behavior with CR-only input. Consequence: valid documents can acquire substantially different block structure. Make line scanning recognize all documented endings and verify affected block consumers with equivalent fixtures. ### 8. Link-label length counts non-ASCII bytes and ignores ordinary ASCII Location: `pulldown-cmark/src/linklabel.rs:122`. Expected: labels contain at most 999 Unicode characters. Observed boundary probes: - 499 `é` characters resolve; 500 do not. - 249 crab emoji resolve; 250 do not. - 1,000 ASCII `a` characters still resolve. The counter increments for every non-ASCII byte and does not increment for ordinary ASCII letters. Consequence: valid internationalized reference labels are rejected, while over-limit ASCII labels are accepted. Count Unicode characters consistently, including escaped and whitespace portions. Add boundary tests for several UTF-8 widths. ### 9. Wikilink source ranges omit the final bracket Location: `pulldown-cmark/src/parse.rs:944`. Expected: `OffsetIter` returns the corresponding complete source range. Observed: `[[Wiki]]` produces link start/end ranges `0..7`, although the construct occupies `0..8`. Embedded wikilink images have the same off-by-one error. Consequence: editors and source transformations leave a bracket behind or select incomplete syntax. Use the end of the second closing delimiter and assert complete ranges for links and images. ### 10. Empty wikilink aliases render delimiter text Location: `pulldown-cmark/src/parse.rs:900`. Expected: closing delimiters remain syntax when handling an empty display label. Observed: `[[Wiki|]]` renders: ```html

]]

``` The selected child starts at a closing-bracket node. Consequence: boundary-case input generates visibly incorrect link text. Handle an empty alias explicitly—either according to a documented empty-label behavior or as literal Markdown—and keep delimiter nodes outside its children. ### 11. Single-character heading attributes are silently dropped Location: `pulldown-cmark/src/firstpass.rs:2548`. heading

`, losing `x`; longer attribute names work. Consequence: callers lose attributes from both parsed events and rendered HTML. Observed: ordinary input `"a\0b"` renders `"

a\0b

\n"`. Consequence: output text contradicts the claimed CommonMark normalization. Normalize literal NUL while preserving source offsets, and add event and renderer regressions. Consequence: future scanner changes lack a written basis for preserving unchecked-access preconditions. Document the bounds, mask, and CPU-feature obligations and justify each unsafe call. This concerns renderer consistency; CommonMark leaves info-string rendering discretionary. ### 15. Public documentation has omissions and an incorrect punctuation example Locations: `pulldown-cmark/src/parse.rs:181`, `pulldown-cmark/src/html.rs:590`, `:625`, `pulldown-cmark/src/lib.rs:674`. exit_code=0 Active time: 8.2 of 2700 seconds; slot waits excluded. Found **14 correctness/build issues**. The existing test suites pass, but added local regressions reproduce the failures below. All behavioral findings are supported by executed tests and source inspection. 1. **HTML blocks ignore valid closing tags.** [firstpass.rs:1250](/work/crate/pulldown-cmark/src/firstpass.rs:1250) uses a case-sensitive search for the opening tag’s corresponding closing tag. CommonMark permits case-insensitive closing tags and, for these blocks, does not require matching tag names. Both `\n\nafter` and `
\nx\n\n\nafter` incorrectly absorb `after` into the HTML block instead of emitting `
after
`. Ordinary documents can lose Markdown rendering for their remaining content.

2. **A trailing tab prevents a code fence from closing.** [scanners.rs:528](/work/crate/pulldown-cmark/src/scanners.rs:528) accepts only spaces after closing backticks. CommonMark permits spaces or tabs. For `"```\nx\n```\t\nafter"`, the closing fence and `after` become code content. A trailing editor-inserted tab can therefore change the rest of a document’s structure.

3. **The CLI renders previous files again when given multiple files.** [main.rs:173](/work/crate/pulldown-cmark/src/main.rs:173) appends every file to the same `String`, then renders that accumulated string on every iteration. Files containing `"one\n"` and `"two\n"` produce:
   ```html
   
one

   
one
   two

   ```
   Expected behavior is to render each input once. Batch callers receive duplicated content and potentially changed Markdown structure.

4. **The CLI silently discards I/O failures.** [main.rs:184](/work/crate/pulldown-cmark/src/main.rs:184) ignores stdin read errors; [main.rs:219](/work/crate/pulldown-cmark/src/main.rs:219) ignores rendering/write errors. Tests supplying invalid UTF-8 through stdin and closing the stdout pipe both observed exit status **0**, with no diagnostic. Callers cannot distinguish successful conversion from missing output.

5. **Case-insensitive footnote references produce inconsistent anchors and numbers.** [html.rs:141](/work/crate/pulldown-cmark/src/html.rs:141) and [html.rs:382](/work/crate/pulldown-cmark/src/html.rs:382) use the original, case-sensitive label strings, although parser lookup folds case. With `a[^NOTE] b[^note]\n\n[^Note]: text\n`, the references target `#NOTE` and `#note`, numbered 1 and 2; the definition has ID `Note`, numbered 3. Recognized references should share a number and resolve to their definition. Instead, ordinary case variations produce broken navigation.

6. **CRLF becomes two spaces inside code spans.** [parse.rs:1340](/work/crate/pulldown-cmark/src/parse.rs:1340) processes CR and LF separately. CommonMark defines CRLF as one line ending, replaced by one space in code spans. Parsing `` `a\r\nb` `` produces `a  b` instead of `a b`. This changes literal code content in Windows-formatted Markdown.

7. **Several block parsers do not recognize CR-only line endings.** [scanners.rs:508](/work/crate/pulldown-cmark/src/scanners.rs:508) searches only for LF. CommonMark also recognizes standalone CR. For example, `"```rust\rx\r```"` becomes a paragraph followed by an empty code block instead of a Rust code block containing `x`. Indented blocks also retain subsequent indentation incorrectly. Equivalent supported line endings should preserve document structure.

8. **The `getopts` feature can select a binary that cannot compile.** [main.rs:25](/work/crate/pulldown-cmark/src/main.rs:25) imports `html` unconditionally, while [Cargo.toml:27](/work/crate/pulldown-cmark/Cargo.toml:27) requires only `getopts` for the binary. `cargo check --locked -p pulldown-cmark --no-default-features --features getopts` fails with E0432 because `html` is disabled. The same configuration with `--lib` passes, isolating the failure to binary feature configuration.

9. **Link-label length counting rejects valid Unicode labels and accepts oversized ASCII labels.** [linklabel.rs:122](/work/crate/pulldown-cmark/src/linklabel.rs:122) increments the character count for each non-ASCII byte and skips ordinary ASCII characters. CommonMark permits at most 999 Unicode code points. A reference label containing 500 `é` characters fails to resolve, while one containing 1,000 ASCII `a` characters resolves. Controls with 499 `é` and 999 ASCII characters pass.

10. **Wikilink source ranges omit the final bracket.** [parse.rs:944](/work/crate/pulldown-cmark/src/parse.rs:944) sets the end offset one byte too early. For `[[page]]`, the link’s range selects `[[page]`. `into_offset_iter()` promises the corresponding Markdown source range; editors and source transformations using this range leave a closing bracket behind.

11. **ATX heading closers mishandle tabs.** [firstpass.rs:1655](/work/crate/pulldown-cmark/src/firstpass.rs:1655) and [firstpass.rs:1664](/work/crate/pulldown-cmark/src/firstpass.rs:1664) trim/check spaces without tabs. CommonMark permits tabs around closing hashes. `"# foo\t###\t\n"` renders `
foo\t###\t
` instead of `
foo
`, exposing syntax characters as heading content.

12. **Inline links accept a title without the required separator.** [parse.rs:1156](/work/crate/pulldown-cmark/src/parse.rs:1156) attempts title parsing even when no whitespace follows a nonempty destination. CommonMark requires separation between destination and title. `[a]("title")` incorrectly emits a link with destination `url` and title `title`; it should not emit a link. The whitespace-separated control behaves correctly.

13. **Subscript parsing can disable unrelated superscript parsing.** [parse.rs:1596](/work/crate/pulldown-cmark/src/parse.rs:1596) and [parse.rs:1614](/work/crate/pulldown-cmark/src/parse.rs:1614) share a delimiter-search lower bound between carets and tildes. With superscript alone, `^a b~ c^` produces `a b~ c`. Enabling subscript as well makes the entire expression literal. An unmatched tilde should not invalidate the independent caret pair; combining documented extensions changes otherwise valid formatting.

14. **Single-character heading attributes disappear.** [firstpass.rs:2548](/work/crate/pulldown-cmark/src/firstpass.rs:2548) skips every attribute token of length one. The public heading-attribute contract permits custom attributes without values. With `ENABLE_HEADING_ATTRIBUTES`, `# hi {x}` should retain `("x", None)`, but emits an empty attribute list. Callers silently lose requested metadata.

one

one\ntwo

\n`, duplicating the first document. Each file should be rendered once. 2. **CLI I/O failures return success** — [main.rs:184](/work/crate/pulldown-cmark/src/main.rs:184), [main.rs:219](/work/crate/pulldown-cmark/src/main.rs:219). Invalid UTF-8 on stdin produces empty output, no diagnostic and exit status 0. Writing to a closed output pipe also exits 0. Read/write failures should propagate so callers can detect lost input or output; buffered output also needs an explicit checked flush. 3. **Linking a wiki image corrupts its destination** — [parse.rs:642](/work/crate/pulldown-cmark/src/parse.rs:642). With `ENABLE_WIKILINKS`, `[![[foo.png]]](bar)` should produce an image linking to `bar`. Instead it produces `

[

`. The successful wikilink path leaves regular bracket-stack entries available for subsequent parsing, allowing the image node to be overwritten. 4. **Uppercase HTML closing tags fail to end blocks** — [firstpass.rs:1250](/work/crate/pulldown-cmark/src/firstpass.rs:1250). CommonMark requires case-insensitive matching here, but termination uses case-sensitive `contains`. For `
\nx\n
\n*after*\n`, `*after*` remains raw HTML-block content instead of becoming an emphasized paragraph. Subsequent document content can be misparsed. 5. **Tabs prevent code fences from closing** — [scanners.rs:528](/work/crate/pulldown-cmark/src/scanners.rs:528). CommonMark permits spaces or tabs after a closing fence; this scanner accepts only spaces. For `"```\nx\n```\t\nafter\n"`, the closing fence and `after` remain inside the code block instead of ending it and starting a paragraph. 6. **Case-insensitive footnote matching produces broken links and numbering** — [html.rs:138](/work/crate/pulldown-cmark/src/html.rs:138). The parser accepts `[^A]` and `[^a]` against definition `[^a]: definition` through case-folded lookup. The renderer nevertheless emits targets `#A` and `#a`, numbers them 1 and 2, and labels the sole definition 2. Both references should share a number and resolve to the same definition. 7. **The `getopts` feature can select an unbuildable binary** — [main.rs:25](/work/crate/pulldown-cmark/src/main.rs:25). The binary requires `getopts` in the manifest but unconditionally imports feature-gated `html`. `cargo check --locked -p pulldown-cmark --no-default-features --features getopts` fails with E0432. The binary’s feature requirements should include its HTML dependency. 8. **An unmatched caret cancels valid strikethrough** — [parse.rs:1614](/work/crate/pulldown-cmark/src/parse.rs:1614). Carets and tildes share a delimiter-search lower bound. With superscript and strikethrough enabled, `~~a b^ c~~` renders literally; it should render `a b^ c`. Attempting to close unmatched superscript incorrectly excludes an existing tilde opener. 9. **Subscript alone suppresses unrelated inline parsing** — [parse.rs:993](/work/crate/pulldown-cmark/src/parse.rs:993). With only `ENABLE_SUBSCRIPT`, `~~*a*~~`, `~~[a](b)~~` and ``~~`a`~~`` all render literally. Unsupported double-tilde delimiters should remain text while their contents retain ordinary emphasis, link and code parsing. Creating a text node with children causes those children to be skipped. 10. **CRLF becomes two spaces inside code spans** — [parse.rs:1340](/work/crate/pulldown-cmark/src/parse.rs:1340). CommonMark treats CRLF as one line ending. `` `a\r\nb` `` yields code text `a b`, whereas LF and CR versions yield `a b`. Each byte is replaced separately, changing code content in ordinary Windows-format documents. 11. **CR-only line endings break block parsing** — [scanners.rs:508](/work/crate/pulldown-cmark/src/scanners.rs:508). `scan_nextline` searches only for LF, although CommonMark also recognizes standalone CR. For example, `" x\r\rafter\r"` becomes one code block containing `after`, rather than a code block followed by a paragraph. Fenced-code and HTML-block probes also fail; LF and CRLF controls pass. 12. **Wikilink source ranges omit the final bracket** — [parse.rs:944](/work/crate/pulldown-cmark/src/parse.rs:944). `[[page]]` has eight bytes, but its start/end link events report `0..7`. Piped links and wiki images have the same error. The documented corresponding-source-range contract requires the complete construct; source-based editing can otherwise leave a stray bracket. 13. **Reference-label length counts bytes incorrectly** — [linklabel.rs:122](/work/crate/pulldown-cmark/src/linklabel.rs:122). CommonMark permits at most 999 characters. Ordinary ASCII characters are not counted, while every non-ASCII UTF-8 byte is counted. A 1,000-character ASCII label is accepted; valid labels containing 500 `é` characters or 334 `界` characters are rejected, leaving links and definitions as literal text. 14. **Tabs are not trimmed around ATX closing markers** — [firstpass.rs:1655](/work/crate/pulldown-cmark/src/firstpass.rs:1655). CommonMark permits tabs around closing hashes and strips trailing tabs. Both `# heading\t###` and `# heading ###\t` retain literal hashes in the heading. The trimming logic recognizes spaces only. 15. **Tabs incorrectly create hard line breaks** — [firstpass.rs:849](/work/crate/pulldown-cmark/src/firstpass.rs:849). Hard breaks require two spaces or a backslash, but the implementation counts all non-newline ASCII whitespace. `foo\t\t\nbar`, `foo \t\nbar` and `foo\t \nbar` each produce `
` instead of a soft break, changing document layout. 16. **Valid HTML with tab-separated unquoted attributes is escaped** — [scanners.rs:452](/work/crate/pulldown-cmark/src/scanners.rs:452). Tabs must terminate an unquoted attribute value. For `a z`, the opening tag becomes `<b x=one\ty=two>` while the closing tag remains HTML. Valid embedded markup is rendered as text because the value scanner consumes the tab. 17. **Invalid table alignment syntax becomes a table** — [scanners.rs:675](/work/crate/pulldown-cmark/src/scanners.rs:675). The bundled GFM contract permits colons only at delimiter-cell edges. A delimiter cell `-:-` is nevertheless accepted as right-aligned. Ordinary prose or an incomplete table containing that sequence is converted into a table instead of remaining text. 18. **Single-character valueless heading attributes disappear** — [firstpass.rs:2548](/work/crate/pulldown-cmark/src/firstpass.rs:2548). With heading attributes enabled, `# heading {a bb c=d}` emits `bb="" c="d"` but drops `a`. The documented custom-attribute syntax does not impose a two-character minimum. Callers silently lose an explicitly supplied attribute. 19. **Tabbed fence metadata leaks into the language class** — [html.rs:261](/work/crate/pulldown-cmark/src/html.rs:261). The renderer’s first-word language convention splits only on spaces. A fence with info `rust\tmore` produces `class="language-rust\tmore"` instead of `class="language-rust"`, turning following metadata into an additional HTML class.
